title: Platform operator reskilling and automation roadmap: 2027-2028
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview

Purpose: This roadmap describes a 3-phase plan (Pilot, Scale, Stabilize) to reskill platform operators and automate routine oncall/runbook tasks with the twin goals of reducing mean time to remediate (MTTR) for LLM-inference incidents and lowering cognitive load for operators. It combines training sprints, tooling work, and new dashboard/alert standards so that operator skill development and automation reinforce each other.

Scope: eng-platform operator team, platform-operator tooling, dashboards and alerts, runbook templates, training labs, and hiring/onboarding. Not in scope: external customer runbooks, product-facing docs, and proprietary customer remediation flows.

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce average platform MTTR for high-severity LLM inference incidents from current baseline by 30% within 6 months of Phase 2 completion.
- Automate detection + remediation playbooks for the top 5 recurring incident classes (token cost spikes, prefix-cache thrash, GPU OOM, regional latency surge, model-variant fallback misfires).
- Certify 80% of platform operators to Level 2 (can lead a 2-hour incident play) in the new operator certification within 9 months.

Success metrics and KPIs
- MTTR per incident class (minutes) — tracked weekly. Target: -30% by Q3 2028.
- Automated remediation rate (incidents fully resolved by automation) — target >= 40% for Tier-1 incidents.
- Operator certification pass rate (%) and time-to-certification (weeks).
- Oncall saturation index (avg alerts/hour/operator) — target <= 0.6 sustained.

Timeline and phases (high level)
- Phase 0 — Prep (Dec 2026): align stakeholders, inventory runbooks, baseline metrics, and create training curriculum.
- Phase 1 — Pilot (Jan 2027 - Apr 2027): run 6-week skill sprints with 2 pilot teams, build 3 automation prototypes (prefetch validator, prefix cache auto-throttle, automated model swap rollback), and ship dashboard templates.
- Phase 2 — Scale (May 2027 - Nov 2027): roll automation to all regions, integrate automation into runbook runner, certify operators, and add SLI/SLO dashboards.
- Phase 3 — Stabilize (Dec 2027 - Mar 2028): focus on reliability, observability debt, and retrospective-driven improvements; measure impact and determine next roadmap.

Milestone table (text):
- M0 (2026-12): Runbook inventory completed; baseline MTTR collected.
- M1 (2027-04): Pilot automations deployed to staging; first 2 operator sprints completed; dashboard template v1.
- M2 (2027-08): Automated remediation for top-3 incident classes in prod; 50% operator certs.
- M3 (2028-03): SLOs revalidated; MTTR target review; roadmap decision for 2028-2029.

Deliverables per phase
- Phase 1: runbook inventory, 3 automation prototypes (each with unit tests and playbook docs), pilot syllabus, dashboard template v1 (SLO + action links).
- Phase 2: runbook-runner integration, automation policy library, canary playbook for automation, training portal with quizzes and labs, alert tuning guidelines.
- Phase 3: operationalization checklist, SLI heatmap dashboard, post-certification mentoring program, retrospective report.

Ownership and roles (who does what)
- Program Lead: Aisha Raman — roadmap coordination, stakeholder alignment, reporting.
- Automation Lead: Diego Morales — design/implementation of runbook automations and developer API.
- Observability Lead: Lina Chen — dashboards, SLI definitions, alert playbooks.
- Training SME: Marcus Patel — curriculum, labs, certification.
- Platform Ops Squad(s): execute sprints, participate in canaries, provide feedback.

Standards: dashboard and alert contract (short)
- All SLO dashboards must include: SLO line, burn rate widget, recent-degradations list, top-5 contributing traces (by cost/latency), and direct links to the canonical runbook.
- Alerts should be actionable: each alert must map to a runbook ID and include severity, suggested next steps, and automation prerequisite flag.
- Naming convention: alert names use the pattern: PLAT.<component>.<class>.<severity> (e.g., PLAT.kv-cache.thrashing.P1).

Runbook automation design patterns (examples)
1) Safe auto-remediate (prefetch limiter)
- Trigger: sustained prefetch TTL increase > 3x baseline for 3m.
- Action: apply soft throttle policy for the affected tenant cohort; post action add annotation with automation run id.
- Safety gates: dry-run for first 5 occurrences, operator approval if changes affect >15% of tenant traffic.

2) Observability-first rollback (model variant swap)
- Trigger: new model variant rollout causes immediate 95th percentile token latency increase > 40% relative to baseline in canary cohort.
- Action: automated rollback to previous variant; create incident ticket with logs and rerun small synthetic test.
- Safety gates: require canary pass threshold configured in rollout policy.

Procedural checklist (operator-facing)
1) Preflight (before any automation deploy):
   - Verify runbook inventory and link IDs.
   - Ensure metrics consumers configured (token-latency, kv-hit-rate, prefetch-ops).
   - Confirm automated test harness (synthetic scenario runner) is green.
2) Canary rollout (3-step):
   - Alpha: deploy automation in staging with synthetic load.
   - Beta: enable automation in canary region (1% traffic) with operator alerting to monitor.
   - GA: enable in all regions with automatic enablement only if Beta metrics stable for 48h.
3) Post-deploy: review automation runbook logs weekly for 4 weeks and collect operator feedback.

Runbook fragment (example)
- Title: Prefix cache thrash: auto-throttle and rewarm
- Symptoms: erratic cache hit-rate drop (>20pp) and token cost spike > 30% sustained for 5m.
- Steps:
  1) Check cache hit-rate dashboard widget and recent eviction traces.
  2) If automation enabled, review automation run id via: rbxctl runbook-runs show <run-id>
  3) To run manual throttle: rbxctl kv prefetch-throttle --cohort <cohort-id> --scale 0.6
  4) To rewarm: rbxctl kv prefetch-rewarm --cohort <cohort-id> --preset hot-90

Example alert rule (YAML snippet)
- alert: PLAT.prefix-cache.thrashing.P1
  expr: |
    increase(prefix_cache.evictions_total[5m]) / increase(prefix_cache.requests_total[5m]) > 0.20
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: "Prefix cache eviction ratio >20% for 5m"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/prefix-cache-thrash-runbook-2027"

Dashboard widget spec (text table)
- Widget: Prefix Cache Health
  - Metrics: cache_hit_rate_5m, eviction_rate_5m, avg_token_latency_1m
  - Visuals: stacked area for hit/evict, single stat for avg latency, recent automation runs table
  - Action: link to runbook + rbxctl quick actions (throttle, rewarm)

Training & certification plan (outline)
- 6-week operator sprint (weekly cadence):
  - Week 1: systems map & incident taxonomy (lectures + lab).
  - Week 2: observability deep-dive + dashboard building lab.
  - Week 3: automation primitives (rbxctl, runbook-runner) + lab.
  - Week 4: synthetic incident day (chaos + safe remediations).
  - Week 5: exam & curated failure postmortem.
  - Week 6: certification exercise (hands-on incident run).
- Certification levels: Level 1 (familiar), Level 2 (lead incident tabletop), Level 3 (mentor + automation author).

Operator tooling checklist (minimum viable)
- rbxctl v1.8+ with runbook-runner plugin
- runbook-runner deployed to staging and canary
- automation policy store (git-backed) with CI checks
- synthetic scenario runner and lab harness
- centralized automation audit log (immutable for 90d)

Canary and rollback policy (short)
- Canary window: 48h minimum; require stability on SLI set (latency, error-rate, cost) for 48h.
- Immediate rollback triggers: 95p latency regresses by >30% OR error-rate doubles OR automation causes >5% tenant impact.
- Operator override: any operator may flip automation flag to manual with justification logged.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: automation misapplies to the wrong tenant cohort. Mitigation: cohort validation step and soft-run mode before enforcement.
- Risk: operator skill friction. Mitigation: pairing sessions, mentoring, and recorded labs.
- Risk: observability gaps hide regressions. Mitigation: mandatory SLI checklist and telemetry sanity tests during CI.

Retro & measurement cadence
- Weekly: automation runbook health digest and top 5 false positives/negatives.
- Monthly: operator certification progress and MTTR trend review.
- Quarterly: full retrospective with sample incidents and roadmap adjustment.

Appendix (references and examples)
- CLI examples: rbxctl runbook-runner apply --policy policies/prefetch-throttle.yaml
- Example policy (text): name: prefetch-throttle
  conditions: [prefetch_eviction_ratio>0.2]
  action: throttle_cohort
- Links: runbook templates (/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks), dashboard templates (/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts), training portal (internal LMS link).

Next steps (immediate)
1) Approve Phase 1 budget and allocate 2 pilot squads by 2026-12-15.
2) Program Lead to schedule stakeholder kickoff and create Phase 1 Jira epic.
3) Observability Lead to publish dashboard template v1 by 2027-01-10.
